interface.title: Narrative Resonance
interface.field: Digital humanities / computational literary studies (emotion and sentiment analysis of prose)
interface.stage_of_work: Exploratory analysis and visualisation of single passages
interface.what_it_is_for: Paste a prose passage and press Read to score it against 12 emotions. You get a whole-text fingerprint strip, a colour palette, a ranked breakdown with the dominant emotion, a per-sentence emotional arc chart, and the text re-rendered with emotion shading and highlighted keywords.

data.note: Three built-in example passages are offered as chips (Nostalgia, Dread, Turning), and the hero area shows a fixed demo fingerprint. I also typed one passage of my own (calm → anger → a negated 'not happy' → sorrow and hope) to test negation handling. All passages were 3 to 5 sentences long. There were no upload or download paths. The only export is a clipboard copy of the palette as CSS variables.

features.name: Sequence fingerprint strip with hover detail
features.general: Summarise an ordered sequence of items as one horizontal strip of coloured segments. Each segment's colour is its category's fixed colour and its opacity shows intensity. A legend and per-segment hover give the category and score.
features.specific: The Fingerprint bar showed one segment per sentence for the 3–5 sentence passages tried. Each segment is filled with the dominant emotion's fixed display colour, and intensity sets its opacity (fingerprint.py:58,88-92 per the reviewer; valence is not used — the saturation/lightness note in the sidebar describes the palette, not the strip). A legend of emotions sits below it, and the tooltip (an SVG <title>, not visible in screenshots) reads e.g. 'Melancholy · intensity 20%'. Texts can only be compared by running them one after another.
steps: Run an analysis (example chip or Read →)
Scan the strip's colour sequence against the legend
Hover a segment to read its emotion and intensity
Load another passage and look at its strip separately
serves_tasks: See the emotional shape of the whole passage at a glance, and compare texts by analysing them one after another

features.name: Sized colour palette with CSS-variable export
features.general: Derive N representative colours from an analysed item, show them as hex-labelled swatches, let the user choose N with a slider, and copy the palette as code.
features.specific: Palette swatches with hex codes. The sidebar 'Palette size' slider (3–8) regenerates them, and the 'Copy as CSS variables' expander shows a :root{--palette-n} block with a copy-to-clipboard button.
steps: Analyse a passage
Set Palette size in the sidebar (3–8)
Open 'Copy as CSS variables'
Press the copy button and paste the :root block elsewhere
serves_tasks: Generate a colour palette for the passage's tone and export it

features.name: Category breakdown bars with dominant-category card
features.general: Rank the categories detected in an item as percentage bars and call out the top category and its intensity in a highlighted card.
features.specific: The Breakdown list shows emotion bars with % (e.g. Anger 100%, Melancholy 86%, Calm 64%, Hope 43%). Beside it, the Dominant card shows the emotion name in its colour and '100% intensity'.
steps: Analyse a passage
Read the ranked bars for secondary emotions
Read the Dominant card for the top emotion and its intensity
serves_tasks: Find the dominant emotion and its intensity

features.name: Interactive multi-series arc chart with per-step list
features.general: Plot several category scores over an ordered sequence as smoothed lines. You can hover a position to read every series there, click or double-click legend entries to hide or isolate series, drag a box to zoom, and double-click to reset. An expandable list underneath gives the label and score for each step.
features.specific: Plotly Arc chart with one trace per emotion over S1…Sn (0–100%), plus a 'Sentence-by-sentence' expander listing S#, an emotion badge with percent, and the sentence text.
steps: Hover a sentence position to read all emotion values there
Click a legend item to hide a trace, or double-click to isolate one
Drag a box over a stretch of sentences to zoom, then double-click to reset
Expand 'Sentence-by-sentence' to match peaks to the actual sentences
serves_tasks: Find where emotions rise and fall across the sequence of sentences
List each sentence's label and score

features.name: Annotated text view: segment shading plus keyword highlighting
features.general: Re-render the source text twice: once with each segment tinted by its assigned category, once with only the trigger words highlighted in category colours. Both views give score tooltips on hover, so you can see which words drove each label and whether negated words were ignored.
features.specific: The 'Shaded text' panel tints each sentence by its emotion (title-attribute tooltip e.g. 'Melancholy 100% · Joy 18%'). The 'Keywords' panel highlights lexicon words such as grief, mournful and hope (title-attribute tooltip e.g. 'Joy: 100%'). Tooltips were read from the DOM; screenshots do not show them. Negated words ('not happy') are left unhighlighted.
steps: Analyse a passage
Scan Shaded text to see each sentence's emotion colour
Hover a sentence for its emotion mix
Scan Keywords to see the trigger words and hover one for its scores
Check that negated phrases are not counted
serves_tasks: See each sentence tinted by its emotion, with score details on hover
Identify the lexicon words that triggered each emotion, including how negation is handled

features.name: Example chips plus free-text input with a run button
features.general: Offer one-click sample inputs that fill the input box and run the analysis immediately, alongside a free-text box with an explicit Run button and an empty-input hint.
features.specific: The 'Try:' chips (Nostalgia, Dread, Turning) fill 'Your text' and render results at once. 'Read →' analyses whatever is typed, and with an empty box it shows 'Paste a passage above, or tap an example, then press Read.'
steps: Click an example chip, or type or paste prose
Press Read →
Clear the box and press Read to get the hint
serves_tasks: Load a sample text and analyse it at once

features.name: Analysis-method selector with conditional credential field
features.general: Choose between a fast local method and a remote-API method from a dropdown. Picking the API method reveals a password-style key field, and unavailable methods are hidden with an explanatory note.
features.specific: Sidebar 'Analysis mode' select: 'Fast · keyword lexicon' or 'Precise · Claude API'. Precise reveals an 'Anthropic API key' field ('Your key is used only for this session'). A note says 'Balanced mode is hidden — install torch + transformers to enable it.' All of this was seen only in the accessibility tree. With no key, Read gives no warning and silently uses a local fallback engine (emotion_engine.py:514-518 per the reviewer), so no Claude output was seen.
steps: Open the Analysis mode dropdown
Choose Precise and see the API key field appear
Enter a key and press Read (not done: no key was available)
Switch back to Fast and see the key field disappear
serves_tasks: Switch to an alternative analysis method (unverified: the remote method never ran)
